title: Reduce CUDA graph capture churn with a dynamic shape compatibility layer and KV-cache-safe replays
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: intermittent regressions observed in production where CUDA graph replay would re-capture too often (different shape guards or stale KV cache state), increasing tail latency and causing noisy SLO violations. This PR implements a small compatibility layer that canonicalizes compatible shapes and a KV-cache safe replay path to reduce unnecessary re-captures. Changes: 1) Add cudagraph_compat.h/cpp: heuristics to determine when two shapes are safe to reuse the same capture (prefix compatibility, token axis padding rules, and kv-cache pointer-stability checks). 2) Update cudagraph_manager.py to maintain a compatibility map keyed by a lightweight shape-signature instead of exact tensors; replays check compat map first. 3) Make scheduler.cpp prefer warmup probes for under-utilized kernels and surface a new metric (cudagraph_reuse_ratio) to console. 4) KV cache patch: kv_cache.cc now stamps ephemeral generation IDs into cache metadata so a replay will detect incompatible KV states and fall back without triggering a full capture for nearby shapes. 5) Tests and docs: added focused unit + integration tests and a short doc page with recommended warmup probes and runtime knobs. Rollout plan: staged on Dedicated pools for one week with observability hooks (cudagraph_reuse_ratio, capture_rate, fallback_count). Linear tickets: ENG-6123 (primary), ENG-6198 (follow-up to remove legacy exact-match path). Checklist:
- [x] Core compatibility algorithm implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Integration tests covering replay fallback and KV cache mismatch
- [x] Metrics emitted and dashboard note added
- [x] Bench script to reproduce capture churn
Notes: this is intentionally conservative — we prefer false negatives (not reusing when safe) over false positives that could cause incorrect outputs. We also retained the exact-match capture path behind a feature flag for a quick rollback.

review_conversation: Diego: Can you explain the rationale for the prefix-compat rule? Aisha: Prefix-compat covers the common decode pattern where inputs vary only in trailing padding or short lookahead; it avoids creating a distinct graph per minor sequence-length delta. Lina: The KV-cache generation-id stamp seems safe but we should ensure it doesn't persist across serialization. Aisha: generation-id is ephemeral and excluded from persisted snapshots by the cache serializer; added a unit test to assert this. Vikram: CI GPU integration flaked on the first run (OOM in bench_script) — re-ran with larger instance and pushed a small guard to limit max-warmup-batch in bench. Diego: Approved after tests and minor doc tweak. Merge performed with squash-merge.
release_notes: Reduced CUDA graph re-captures by introducing a dynamic shape compatibility layer and KV-cache-safe replay path; emits new metric cudagraph_reuse_ratio; conservative default behavior with a feature flag for exact-match fallback.
patch_snippet:
--- runtime/cudagraph_manager.py (new) +++
+def shape_signature(tensor_shape, kv_meta):
+    # lightweight canonical signature: (batch, effective_seq_bucket) + kv generation mask
+    bucket = (tensor_shape[1] + 7) // 8  # 8-token buckets
+    gen_mask = kv_meta.get("gen", 0) & 0xff
+    return f"b{tensor_shape[0]}_s{bucket}_g{gen_mask}"
tests_summary: Added unit tests for shape_signature equivalence classes, integration test that simulates alternating shapes and verifies reuse ratio > 80% under bench workload, and a KV cache mismatch test that asserts safe fallback without capture when generation-id mismatch occurs.
notes_for_operators: Feature flag: runtime.cudagraph.exact_match_fallback=true/false (default: false). If you see unexpected output regressions after enabling, flip flag off to revert to exact-match captures. Monitor cudagraph_reuse_ratio and fallback_count. If fallback_count spikes > 5% of captures, enable additional warmup probes or increase capture-bucket granularity.
motivation_summary: Reduce tail latency and SLO noise caused by excessive CUDA graph re-captures due to near-identical shapes or transient KV cache differences. This improves throughput stability with minimal risk to output correctness.
